notes.title: Update 1.0.5 – From Developers, With Love ❤️
notes.content:
Happy Valentine's Day, colonists! 💌 While we can’t send you chocolates or flowers, we can send you a fresh batch of fixes and improvements, straight from our hearts. 💖

Nothing says true love like a bug-free colony, right? So, we polished things up, removed some unfortunate softlocks, and made sure your lasers of love (or logistics) keep flowing smoothly.

[i]Roses are red, our lasers are too, we fixed some bugs… all just for you! 💘[/i]
No more accidental endings, unboosted buildings, or text misadventures. Now go forth and terraform with love!

[h3]💘 Changelog – Because We Care 💘[/h3]

❤️ Fixed a game triggering the victory screen too early after loading the game in the final phases. You should be able to load previous saves without triggering the ending early.
❤️ Fixed an issue with boosters where they were not affecting buildings that were placed after the booster was placed.
❤️ Fixed resource production tooltip showing a bugged-out icon whenever the tooltip opened for the first time after starting the game.
❤️ Fixed player being able to place a charcoal production building in the prologue and softlocking themselves if they reaaally wanted to.
❤️ Fixed 5 instances of text/UI clipping across the game for some languages that had longer text values.

Now, go forth and spread the love of colony-building, lasers, and resource logistics. Thanks for playing Scorchlands, and as always – your feedback is our Valentine. 💝

🔥 May your lasers stay bright, your resources flow smoothly, and your colonies thrive! 🚀💛

notes.title: Weirdly Satisfying Colony Management💎⚡
notes.content:
[h2]Hey, fellow gamers![/h2]

[h3]Have you ever stumbled upon a game that seems like it was made just for you, but somehow nobody's talking about it? [/h3]
[h3]Yeah, that’s [b]Scorchlands[/b] – a cozy, strategic, resource-optimizing dream wrapped up in lasers, hexagons, and adorable bird-folk.[/h3]

[h2]Let’s be real for a second.[/h2]

Somehow, this little game of ours ended up being really well-loved. And it turns out people really like it – Scorchlands has [b]95%[/b] positive reviews on Steam 👍, and the players who find it tend to get… well, hooked for hours. It’s a unique mix of colony-building, resource logistics, and puzzle-like combat, all without the usual stress of strategy games. If you love tinkering, optimizing, and making the perfect production web, this might just be your next addiction.

But here’s the problem:
Not enough people know about it. And that, dear reader, is where you come in.

[h2]What makes Scorchlands special?[/h2]
🦜 Relaxing, but deeply strategic – No timers, no pressure. Just pure optimization bliss.
🔬 Hex-based city-building with real resource logistics – Lasers and mirrors replace conveyor belts, and yes, it gets wild.
🌎 Terraforming & biome placement – Unlock and move entire biomes to shape your perfect colony.
🧩 Combat? More like a puzzle challenge – No base defense, no raids, just tactical positioning and problem-solving.
🛠️ Total freedom in how you build – No storage buildings, no wasted space, just raw efficiency (or chaos, your call).
🤯 No chain-reaction collapses – Mess up your supply chain? Fix it without losing everything.
🔍 Exploration actually matters – Find creative paths around enemies and solve fights before they even start.
💡 Endless tinkering potential – The deeper you go, the more satisfying the logistics get.

[previewyoutube=y1ZWLgdJT7s;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]We’re doing something special.[/h2]
To celebrate the amazing players who already love Scorchlands, and to finally let more people discover it, we’re running a big discount event 💰, and yes – the free demo 🎮 is back! Because the best way to know if a game is for you is to just try it.

[h2]So, what’s next?[/h2]
Give the demo a spin. Tell a friend. Or don’t – just optimize your colony in solitude like a true logistics mastermind. Either way, Scorchlands is here, waiting for you to fall into its hexagonal trap of laser-powered perfection.

Get comfy in Scorchlands – manage resources, your way! 💎⚙️
c.u!

notes.content:
Hi Birdfolks! 🐦

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/e53ca2f19f727a24d3f67b6fe2a5f5b3b9db612b.png[/img]

We are proud to announce that the full release of Scorchlands is out now! After many months of development in Early Access, with 95% positive reviews on Steam, we’re more than ready for the final launch. [b]You can grab Scorchlands 1.0 version at a great price 5,99$![/b]

We couldn’t have done it without your support! Thank you so much for all the feedback we’ve received from you and for your positive response to our project. We have read it all and 90% of it made its way to the game! We could say that you helped us hatch! 🐣

[b]The demo version has also been updated, so if you’d like to try Scorchlands first and see if it’s a game for you, make sure to download it from our Steam page![/b]

Below you can see our completely NEW trailer celebrating the launch. Enjoy!

[previewyoutube=y1ZWLgdJT7s;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re new to Scorchlands, here is what you should know about the key game features:

[list]
[*] Hex grid-based city-building – construct various buildings in your colonies. Each structure's productivity depends on neighboring resources and other constructions.
[*] Complex resource management – it’s not only about extracting materials. Scorchlands takes account of logistics – the movement of resources between colonies and combining them in robust processing chains. And yes, we move resources using LASERS!
[*] Terraforming for the greater good – use magic and technology to change the biomes on procedurally generated maps and exploit the new environment to gain its unique resources
[*] Technology designed to give fun – there’s no fun in a sandbox if you don’t have the toys to play with. The technology system in Scorchlands is key for player progression and new discoveries open up new ways to play with the game world
[*] Minimalistic combat system – when you get into a fight, positioning will be the key. Destroy your enemies by surrounding them and placing your forces in optimal locations.
[/list]

And for the gamers that are regularly checking our updates, we have a reminder about all the new features available now in the final version of the game:

[list]
[*] Introduced endgame
[*] Achievements
[*] Controller support
[*] Customizable difficulty

[h1]Full Changelog:[/h1]

[b]Big changes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Player can now zoom out 20% further before going to overview mode.
[*] Added an option in settings to completely block auto transition to overview mode when zooming out.
[*] Added an option to build over existing structures by holding Ctrl.
[*] Added an option to cycle through alternative production recipes by pressing Tab.
[*] Improved the general quality of Chinese localization.
[*] Added more dioramas in the main menu. Now the game remembers how far the player got and when starting the game, displays an appropriate diorama.
[*] Overhauled the visuals of the decorative villagers present across the colonies.
[*] Added an option to fast travel through pipelines. This works similarly to laser fast travel, but with an extra twist.
[/list]
[b]Improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*] Increased the threshold before auto transitioning to overview mode when zooming out. This will help avoid accidentally going to overview.
[*] Completed missions are now moved below missions yet to be done in the list at the bottom left corner of the screen.
[*] Colony placement sound has been made ~25% more silent.
[*] Colony placement animation now only takes 4 seconds to complete (down from 6).
[*] Added rebindable keybinds for rotating camera. By default it's done with ";" and "'".
[*] Added rebindable keybinds for panning camera up and down. By default it's done with "[" and "]".
[*] Improved camera animation when configuring lasers.
[*] Added an option to speed typing animation of a dialogue by clicking while the text is being typed.
[*] Improved the way that cursor icons show mouse buttons to press.
[*] Improved cursor visibility on 4k displays
[*] Added a small cursor hover tooltip showing what a transmutation crystal is currently making.
[*] Removed resolutions below 800x600 from settings as the game was not playable on those.
[*] Removed duplicate resolution options with different screen refresh rates. Now the highest refresh rate is chosen by default.
[*] Improved the quality of dialogue sounds.
[*] Each bird-advisor now has a slightly different voice.
[*] Slightly improved player visibility whenever obscured by an obstacle.
[*] Non-player units are no longer shown when behind obstacles.
[*] Added helpful arrows that show Nexus connection points whenever placing a laser.
[*] Added an option to disable dialogues when starting a new game. Previously this option was available only in settings and was easily missed.
[*] Fixed issues rendering horizon on Linux (previously player occasionally would see a big red dot in the sky).
[/list]
[b]Bugfixes: [/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed some red crystals surrounded by enemies being unprotected.
[*] Fixed player being able to slide around edges of the map over liquids.
[*] Fixed colony upgrade panel not opening properly when first clicking it after the game starts.
[*] Fixed recipe naming of Frostbloom Farming (onsite i regular). Previously it was incorrectly called Caustic Berry Farming.
[*] Fixed camera not returning properly to the original position after the player creates or moves a biome.
[*] Fixed production recipe info panel not closing properly when player approaches a group of enemies.
[*] Fixed an incorrect error popup whenever player selected a unit by clicking on it.
[*] Fixed player units moving slower in formation whenever player was moving on an elevated ground (for example on a desert mountain).
[*] Fixed player being able to run onto flying islands when moving in a formation.
[*] Fixed player not being able to unequip an item when they had exactly 0 available extra pieces.
[*] Fixed Landscaping Bug's Nest behaviour on Snowlands biome.
[*] Fixed Landscaping Bug's Nest behaviour next to Nexus.
[*] Fixed tiles changed by Landscaping Bug's Nest not refreshing properly whenever player bulldozes a Stabilizer that was claiming those tiles.
[*] Fixed a visual issue that could happen when two lasers aimed at each other at a steep angle while bouncing of mirrors.
[*] Fixed player units not being able to find a path over other non-player units.    Previously they could only pathfind through the main hero.
[*] Fixed enemy influence area not being displayed when selecting a unit that stands far away from the enemy group.
[*] Fixed camera sensitivity being dependent on screen resolution. Previously it would be less sensitive for larger displays.
[*] When placing lasers, the arrow that shows their forward direction is now properly rendered over the fog. Previously the arrow would partially disappear next to nexus and on clifflands.
[/list]
[h2]New languages are coming 🐦[/h2]

We want everyone to have a good experience with playing Scorchlands, that’s why we care about adding translations for our launch.

Currently the game supports: English, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Russian.

[b]We plan to add:[/b]

Polish, Japanese, Italian,Spanish - Spain, Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, Greek, Dutch, Indonesian, Korean, Portuguese - Portugal, Romanian, Swedish, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Hungarian, Slovak, Latvian, Arabic, Thai.

notes.title: May the workforce be with you! Early Access Update #08
notes.content:
Hey, Birdfolks! 🐦

A little bird told us that we have some announcements to make! And we are more than happy to share some news with you.

With this update we are introducing a new game mechanic: workforce. And we are sure that you’ll love it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/49e5229047d9b2775433051b7b0d5cc0219bb1da.png[/img]

From now on, each colony will possess a certain amount of workforce! This change will dictate how many buildings your colony can support. Thanks to that, you’ll get some free space, which will help you with the most optimal build. You can build your colony not only faster, but more thoughtful! Also, building neighborhood bonuses is going to be much more impactful! Establishing laser connections is gonna be much easier, too.

By default, a colony starts with [b]16 workforce and if you’d like to increase it, you can either:[/b]

[list]
[*] upgrade colony radius
[*] build more Stabilizers
[/list]

[b]Each population point spent on a colony gives it 8 workforce. That means you can place 8 more buildings![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/ea4409f4bb46cbbf216a57513ba924bdfa2502cf.png[/img]

Any previous saves are compatible with these changes, BUT due to the nature of this update, you might have to do some housekeeping. Buildings over the limit from previous saves won’t be destroyed, but in order to place any new stuff, excess buildings will have to be removed. 

So keep that in mind!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/75263045eb75c59f8f34f77ae83dcaaa53d2baee.png[/img]

[b]But that’s not all![/b]

We changed the balancing of particular buildings and production chains. This way the limiting of the number of buildings won’t stop you from getting the resources that you need!

We know that some of you would like to dive deeper into the changelog, so here is the full list of changes and fixes in this new patch. 

Enjoy!

[b]## [Patch 0.3.1] -- 2024-01-15[/b]

[b]Changes:[/b]

- Colonies become much less prone to having their production thrown off balance whenever a couple of buildings need to be deleted to make some space.
- Graphical performance has improved especially at the later stages of the game.

[b]Fixes:[/b]

- Fixed the bug that would sometimes delete large chunks of nearby colonies whenever destroying an enemy wave.
- Added missing production tree for tier 6.
- Changed the word capitalization for errors and tooltips to make them more readable.
- Removed "Precision Terraforming" technology as it did not work due the building not being in the game yet. 
- Added progress bars to some missions in prologue to make things a bit easier to understand.

We truly believe that this update will highly upgrade your gaming experience with Scorchlands! Let us know what you think, we’re always happy to hear your feedback. Take care and remember, if you want to be up-to-date with everything that’s happening in the nest, make sure to join our Discord server! Check our Facebook, Twitter, TikTok and Instagram, too!

[url=https://discord.gg/J57AeJDMw7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/f59186b8ddb200030bd818ea41f3ebf2deeab473.gif[/img][/url]

See ya and have fun!

notes.title: Let's conquer Snowlands! ❄️ Early Access Big Update 🔧
notes.content:
[h3]Attention, Birdfolks! 🐦[/h3]

We are thrilled to unveil the blazing hot (or cold, but we’ll see about that later ❄️) update for Scorchlands, igniting your gameplay experience to new heights! Brace yourselves for a sizzling adventure as we present a wave of significant changes and great improvements. 

[h3]Pipelines 🔗[/h3]

First of all, we are excited to announce pipelines! Connect colonies, simplify logistics, and balance resources like never before. Just find the right path and make sure that it is not too steep or doesn’t cross with other pipelines. Get ready for a whole new world of possibilities!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/addb1be743394e15c8f3d8cea508fcb43de60a92.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/0c27800e72e413ff65faba8aad9b5a035e613778.png[/img]

[h3]Let it snow… ☃️[/h3]

Another huge addition is the new biome - Snowlands! Experience the power of flux energy as you explore three floating islands with unique resources and mechanics. Prepare to unleash your creativity, but remember… A single colony can only be located on one flying island at once! You have to work wisely! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/d8d5547323e9ec3700c45a8c3ea403aee9dde86a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/15e5639a49d769098eee16e7e3f2a73d82a8cd68.png[/img]

[h3]The end? 👀[/h3]

Did you really think that was it? Oh no - this is the first update from our Road Map after all! Over the past months we've been hard at work bringing you a lot of enhancements and fixes. We've significantly improved movement mechanics and combat. We've even introduced two new units - the Heavy Warrior and the Ranger. You absolutely have to try them out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/1700e11cbbaecfeed858e2b3cd56619d02bafb38.jpg[/img]

That's still not all, though. Get ready for a whole lot of fun with plenty of gameplay improvements. New recipes, enhanced atmosphere, and a bunch of options you've never seen before! We've also addressed numerous bugs that you've kindly reported, and we can't thank you enough for that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/880db4f4b70d8e1143b1b97757a47fa7ef69905d.png[/img]

If you're curious about all the details, make sure to check out the full changelog below:

[b]## [Big Update 0.2.0] - 10.07.2023[/b]

Movement overhaul:
Along with the addition of flying islands, the movement also received a series of improvements.
- In certain situations, players can now go airborne, letting them go over obstacles.
- There is a new special building dedicated purely to movement — Hover Platform.
- When going off a cliff, the main hero will now perform a jump and gain a speed boost.
- Players can now slide on ice tiles.
- And sometimes players can jump to their doom too.
- Main hero received an extra shadow directly below their feet that helps in determining their position over terrain.
Combat:
- Added a new player unit: Heavy warrior. An improved version of Light Warrior.
- Added a new player unit: Ranger. A unit capable of affecting enemies from two tiles away.
- Rebalanced Combat Alchemist. Now they provide even more support, have high defence and some attack.
- Added two new enemies in the snowy biome.
- With the help of newly added units, players should be now able to defeat even the hardest-to-access enemy waves and claim the whole map.
Additions:
- Added an atmospheric distance fog.
- Added a sky that gradually evolves as the day progresses.
- Added 4 new alternative recipes for already present resources aimed at providing alternative ways of producing those resources. These are: Ether, Coal, Tools and Potions.
- Added "Stone Processing" technology to the tech tree unlocked immediately at the start of the game.
- Added an option to go immediately to overview when standing at a waypoint and pressing "E".
- Added an option to enter photo mode from the pause menu.
- Added an option to respawn when stuck from the pause menu.
- Added a soft reverb effect for most environmental audio.
- Added a highlight showing the tile when a mirror will be spawned when placing a mirror catapult.

- Wind audio is now only played when panning the camera around fast — not when standing idle.
- Combined several tabs in the buildings panel at the bottom of the screen.
- Improved the positioning of Transfer Lasers when connected at a steep angle.
- Changed keybind for toggling mission panel on/off from "N" to "O". Change is visible after resetting keybinds.
- Swapped keybinds for opening Tech tree and colony upgrade tab. Change is visible after resetting keybinds.
Fixes:

- Fixed colony placement being cancelled when the player rotated the camera.

- Fixed photo mode turning on when using the shortcut from pause menu or when typing a save name.

We've poured our hearts into making the game even better, and now it's your turn to dive in and experience the thrill. notes.title: Gameplay Insight #4 - Tech Tree 🌳, the Altars System 🕯️ & mod support 🔧
notes.content:
Hello, birdfolks! 👋

How are you doing? We just released the Reveal Date Trailer (Early Access). 📺
In case you didn’t watch it, here it is:

[previewyoutube=5T6kA4BZQsg;full][/previewyoutube]

Today, it’s time to continue our Gameplay Insight series. This is the 4th issue of it! 🎒 We’ll visit three (tree? 🤔) places.

[h3]📡 Tech Tree 🌳[/h3]
Let’s take a quick look at the technology tree. It’s quite sprawling, but what we like about it is that you don’t wait for your technology to be researched. You choose it - you get it. Here’s a screen from the trailer we posted a few lines above.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/2b03586e43624f9c9e8405ef586bae3836d7ee7a.png[/img]

This immediacy is in line with the core idea of Scorchlands, which is playing at your own pace. ♟️

Whenever you make a decision, the game reacts instantly. You don't wait for a production bar to reach its end, or for resources to be slowly, arduously gathered. It's more about thinking about your next move and making it than about going through the motions in order to see it happen. The pacing depends on you alone.

[h3]🐦 The Altars System 🕯️[/h3]
Like in every city-builder, the buildings you place matter a lot. In Scorchlands, some buildings can influence others. 

To create some resources you need to do something more than just provide enough materials or place appropriate buildings. Meet the altars – special buildings influencing other production buildings within their reach. You will need different combinations of altars to create different resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/70b3f4b04dec7c0b29671b92dd7213c3277fffec.png[/img]

There are three types of altars and each has a unique shape of its influence scope. These shapes are not random. They will be easy to use in most cases but if you have limited space in your colony and you don’t want to waste it, or if you want to produce several resources at once, you’ll certainly have to experiment a bit.

[h3]🧰 A few words about mod support 🔧[/h3]

Let us put it this way.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/6d53ab9debe0d4c8c319484c222b29b863589177.png[/img]

Yes, Scorchlands will have mod support from the very beginning – right at the start of Early Access! This is great news for folks that want more stuff or wish to spice up their vanilla game a bit.
Our goal is to make all of the content present in the game with the exception of the core mechanics, moddable. We know that your imagination is boundless and we want to let you go wild with your creations!

[b]👉 Modders will be able to modify and add new types of terrain, biomes, buildings, technologies, and units. New language versions of the base game and mod localisation can be added to both the already existing and the newly introduced content. 👀
[/b]
Of course, we know that at the beginning the mod support won’t be flawless and modders will encounter bugs. However, we can assure you that all will be patched and improved with time. Our team is focused on constantly tweaking things in the game’s EA build.
We can’t wait to see what you’ll cook up! 👨‍🍳

notes.title: Gameplay Insight #3: Terraforming, biomes & resource management 🏗️
notes.content:
Hello, Folks! 👋
We all that Giwis live the rule “can’t stop | won’t stop” and they’re constantly running from one place to another. In this issue of Gameplay Insight, we’ll take on a journey with three stops ahead of us. There’s a lot that needs to be told – put on your running gear and let’s get started! 🏃‍♂️

🚏 Stop no. 1:

[h3]Terraforming[/h3]
In Scorchlands, you reshape the terrain instantly, and anywhere you want. Moreover, later you can relocate the biomes you've made at a whim and any time! You get total control over the terrain you build your cities on. Feel free to do whatever you feel like doing. 🤝

It’s good to think strategically when terraforming. Clever placement of biomes lets you benefit more from their characteristics. We wrote a lot about the bonuses in the second Gameplay Insight – you’ll find it 👉 here.

Let’s get straight to the point - as you develop your civilization, you can progress through multiple biomes, each with different advantages. 

We wanted to make sure that instant terraforming remains fun and special regardless of how many times you do it. To accomplish this, we took a lot of effort to visually represent the process in an awe-inspiring way. Our team decided to choose a pastel color palette 🎨 to play a key role in the graphic design of Scorchlands. The sound plays a big part, too - when you hear the earth crumbling like it’s ready to rearrange itself, you know you’re dealing with a powerful and mysterious force.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/7ed855f0f32eb8b6898b902dddf4e9b413ce7e61.png[/img]

We hope you’ll enjoy changing the landscape and making it your own. Time for the second stop! ✋

🚏 Stop no. 2:

[h3]Biomes[/h3]

Everytime you start your game on a volcanic planet, the terrain surrounding you at the beginning of your journey is a wasteland of scorched land and lava 🔥. Besides this first biome, there are three more you can create later in your game. Just a reminder - each biome introduces a new set of resources, technologies, and a new type of combat equipment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/bf99c12fc41d3e8f32e883ef5c6e60604f4b7075.png[/img]

The placing of a new biome you want to create shouldn’t be random – look for the spot which will produce the best resource veins.

What’s more, you need to plan for the future of your colonies – you would want to place a biome to make the resource transportation much easier rather than more difficult. Keep in mind the already existing terrain. If your new biome overlaps with the one already there, it might destroy the old landscape.

Each new biome introduces a couple of new twists to the city building. You will have to plan around the shape of resource veins, the terrain itself, establish logistic connections between colonies in other biomes and master the production of newly unlocked types of products and finally scale up your infrastructure.

Creating new biomes is essential for gathering new resources and expanding your colony but it’s also fun to see how much you can transform a volcanic 🌋 wasteland!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/aa1c138c0450c175833abe0effd2e6c4bf5f325d.png[/img]

We always have a lot of fun constantly reshaping the hexagons around our colonies – hope you like terraforming the biomes too! Adjust your laces, it’s time for…

🚏 Stop no. 3:

[h3]Resource management[/h3]

To which our game has quite a unique approach. 👀

In Scorchlands, the standard gradual resource production was replaced with a supply and demand system. By producing resources, you simply increase its local availability. Whenever you use up a resource, its demand is increased. Resource deficits can limit the effectiveness of dependent production chains and having a surplus of production means that the resource can still be used for more stuff. 📈

The most interesting aspect of this system is that the player receives instant feedback for every action performed. You can see the changes in resource availability right away and don’t need to wait for anything to be produced.

This also eliminates other forms of waiting. For example, your technological advancement is achieved by continuously scaling up your empire and expanding your production. Any new technology discovered will increase the demand for the required resources. The same stands true whenever creating new biomes or making equipment for your combatants.

The final noteworthy advantage to having no resource storage in Scorchlands is the fact that it reduces the player's mental load. Apart from much faster and smoother gameplay, it lets you focus on other features focused on the supply and demand system that you can't usually find in other city builders or similar games.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1090100/Scorchlands/

This is the last stop. 🚏
See you around!

Keep calm and get ready for Gameplay Insight #4! 🍿
Developers from Ringlab ⚗️

notes.title: Gameplay Insight #2: The Bonus System 🐣
notes.content:
Hello, Folks! 👋

It’s time to change the gear ⚙️ with publishing new announcements on Steam. Today, we’ll focus on the [b]bonus system[/b] that allows the player to make the most out of the colony. But first: check out this photo 📸 of bird colonists just hanging around in the city. We hope that you can feel the heartbeat of the colony! For us, it’s the little details that matter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/99c8eb870e7a0b80dde9ff998835e5a70ddf3a6c.png[/img]

They're not only making the place feel more alive, but also add some extra weight to your actions - structures you build are inhabited, and your decisions impact not only just numbers, but also your Giwis. Let’s leave them now, we’re sure they’re having a great time. 🥳

This time we want to show you our [b]bonus system[/b]. Let’s get straight to it! 💥

In one of the previous posts, we explained that building placement is very important in Scorchlands. There are many reasons for this, such as limited space, resource management, etc. Thinking about your surroundings plays a key role here, but there’s also another important reason.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/bf99c12fc41d3e8f32e883ef5c6e60604f4b7075.png[/img]

[h2]Each production building has its own set of rules specifying the set of conditions where it works at full capacity.[/h2]

Planning out your colony layout is just as much about production management, as it is about maximizing the performance of each individual building. 🗼

Some bonuses can be quite straightforward. How is that? Let us provide some examples: raw resource producers need to be placed next to their desired resource veins, but this is only the tip of the iceberg. Liquid extractors should be placed on the shorelines, which are limited and hard to claim in a single colony. Mineshafts work faster when placed one next to another, however, they still need some unobstructed space to mine. Gatherers need a lot of free land, but with a big area, a few other buildings nearby won't hinder them that much.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/7fc62a2bf1a3cf579249c98f314a2f855710d9e9.jpg[/img]

Buildings that do process complex resources also behave in their own ways. Crafters work best next to raw extraction buildings. Artificer gets boosted by processing buildings, Alchemist profits from Farms and science buildings, etc. Think about your possibilities and the connections you're about to make in your colonies.

[h2]There is no limit on bonuses that one tile can provide.[/h2]

If you find a very rare, but very small resource vein, you can still build and organize a whole colony around it, and use it to the fullest. Thanks to all of this, planning a colony organically turns into an interesting puzzle 🧩. It will never be the same – each colony will differ from one another depending on the available resource veins, resources available or buildings placed.

Dear birdfoks 🐦, that’s all for today. Yes, yes – we know that there's a lot of information above, so keep calm, take your time to fully assimilate the knowledge from this Gameplay Insight.
Until next time my friends!

notes.title: How to build your colony? 🤔
notes.content:
Hello, Folks! 👋

The basis of a city-builder game is - obviously - building a city. [b]Or, like in our case, a network of interdependent colonies. [/b]So, we decided to write a Steam News dedicated to this topic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/cb989238a5e51627543ff01a48ee68655361e2c8.png[/img]

[b]Building placement is an important part of resource management in Scorchlands 🐦[/b], so let’s take a closer look at this aspect of the game. 🔍

When you plan out a new production district or want to set up a connection between two colonies, you’re bound to build a lot.

[h2][b]Good news:[/b] nearly all the buildings are totally free and you place them instantly! What’s more, you can move or destroy them whenever you want. 🎉[/h2]

Thanks to that you can focus on the gameplay and not on gathering resources just to be able to afford a new building.

The only real limit is the borders of your colony, as you can only build inside. Colonies can be expanded to accommodate more buildings as you progress through the tech tree, but there is a limit on the number of colonies and colony upgrades. With that limit in mind, you won’t be able to place all the buildings in just one colony. When you get to that point, you’ll have to decide what to build in each colony and where. 🗺️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41122400/bb6f382afb724e11201f7000da71341a2c3df039.png[/img]

[b]There are many ways you can set up the production of each available resource.[/b]

For example, you can:
[list]
[*] create medium specialized settlements,
[*] spend more resources on creating the main colony and surround it with smaller mining settlements,
[*] create a spaghetti-like mess that will work just fine. 🍝
[/list]
There are lots of different ways to approach organizing the colonies - the player makes important decisions about choosing the resources. All of them have some pros and cons, so choose wisely! ⚖️

Watching the districts and other things grow organically from your actions is one of the most satisfying things in the game.

Do you already have a method you’ll want to try? Remember to wishlist the game, it really helps us out!

notes.title: It's not a bird, it's a Giwi! 🐦
notes.content:
Hello!,

Look! The egg is cracking 🥚! What’s that? Is it a bird 🐣? Is it a human with a beak? Nope, he’s one of the Giwis! 🐦

But before we start, let me introduce myself. I’m Jakub, I’m the developer that created the Birdfolks you see here. The time has come to show you my beloved project named Scorchlands! 🎉

Giwis are the inhabitants of my dreamt world. Bringing them to your PCs will be better with a suitable partner ([url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/StarDrifters]Star Drifters[/url] 🚀), who decided to publish my vision. I’ve got to say I’m super excited about working with them - I’ve got nothing but respect for this Warsaw-based team, they’re also developers and released [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/718650/Driftland_The_Magic_Revival/]Driftland - The Magic Revival [/url]- one of the Polish games that’s close to my heart. 💖

[previewyoutube=bjYEg5katr4;full][/previewyoutube]

If Giwis could Tweet, they would post this ⤵️
Scorchalnds is a game in which you manage production of fantastic resources on a foreign, volcanic moon. Play at your own pace and relax in a setting that combines magic and science.

Unfortunately, Giwis don’t Tweet (just like Machete 😎), but I - catch me here: [url=twitter.com/ringglan]twitter.com/ringglan[/url].

TL;DR - main features of Scorchlands 👀

[list]
[*] Hex grid-based city-building – construct various buildings in your colonies. Each structure's productivity depends on neighboring resources and other constructions.
[*] Complex resource management – it’s not only about extracting materials. Scorchlands takes account of logistics – the movement of resources between colonies and combining them in robust processing chains. And yes, we move resources using LASERS!
[*] Terraforming for the greater good – use magic and technology to change the biomes on procedurally generated maps and exploit the new environment to gain its unique resources
[*] Technology designed to give fun – there’s no fun in a sandbox if you don’t have the toys to play with. The technology system in Scorchlands is key for player progression and new discoveries open up new ways to play with the game world
[*] Minimalistic combat system – when you get into a fight, positioning will be the key. Destroy your enemies by surrounding them and placing your forces in optimal locations.
[/list]
The most important info for now is the fact that…

The demo version will be available on Steam in just a few days! 💪

[b]Say hello to Birdfolks 👋[/b]
Who says magic and science don’t go along? The birdfolk of Giwi are curious explorers and inventors - what better way to satisfy scientific curiosity than an expedition to the moon?

The volcanic satellite, Helia, is filled with resources, so the daring explorers will not only discover new magical technologies but also harvest riches and establish colonies. Great discoveries aren’t easy to come by - the moon’s surface is full of dangerous creatures waiting to fight for their habitat. The Giwi will have to use magic not only to fend off any predators, but also to sustain their economy with arcane lasers allowing them to handle resource logistics by connecting all colonies into an industrial web.

To fully discover the mysteries of Helia players will have to establish multiple colonies on the moon’s surface, discover new tech and magic, terraform the hostile environment and fight against local creatures.

[b]Meet Giwis AND find out why they RUN 🎽[/b]
Although avian looking, Giwi are flightless -- they have arms in place of wings, no really distinctly developed keel bone and mostly upright body posture. Their bodies are feathered, except their forearms and lower legs, which are scaled, have talons and are frail-looking (similarly to regular bird’s legs). Their heads also resemble the head of a bird.

The Giwi are actually pretty early in civilization/technology state: think what would happen if humans discovered overpowered electricity in the year 500 BC and 200-300 would have passed.

Below are some common traits that are often present among many of Giwis 👀:
[list]
[*] tricky, reckless - they do not think things through often enough
[*] crafty - they appear capable of making crazy contraptions or overdoing things in funny ways
[*] harmless looking - even when it tries to, does not look like a badass
[*] animal-like, cute design that resembles household pets nobody would ever hurt.
[/list]
